citrate.src_dG: bounded above in strength by the thiolate isotherm free energies on Au (Dinkel 2016 -0.48 eV, Dinkel 2018 -0.41 eV on 5 nm NPs): carboxylate binds more weakly than thiolate and is displaced by thiols; Ag stronger than Au by the DFT O/halide binding offset (OH, Cl: Ag - Au = -0.6..-0.7 eV in vacuum, scaled down for solvation): judgement
citrate.src_shell: dense layer ~1.0 nm (Park & Shumaker-Parry 2014) to solvated shell ~2 nm (Cardenas Lopez 2022)

tannic.src_dG: per molecule: multidentate galloyl/phenol binding; single phenol/benzene on Au(111)/Ag(111) -0.64..-0.97 eV in vacuum with vdW-DFT, reduced by water displacement; weak
tannic.src_shell: TA molecule ~2 nm; 3.0 nm vendor hydrodynamic shell is an upper bound

pvp.src_dG: per repeat unit (carbonyl O-metal + vdW, weak per unit, strong per chain); Ag(100) > Ag(111) qualitatively (Al-Saidi 2012); judgement, weak
pvp.src_shell: adsorbed PVP loops/tails, judgement (2-4 nm for 10-55 kDa PVP)

ctab.src_dG: Br- headgroup layer: vacuum DFT Br on Au(111) -0.99 eV, Ag(111) -1.54 eV (vs 1/2 Br2), strongly reduced by hydration; bilayer cooperativity; judgement, weak

sources: DLVO + Fuchs stability ratio for bare charged 1.5-3 nm clusters (this work): 1/W median 1.197 (16-84 %: 1.0-1.307), max barrier 0.2 kT -> no electrostatic barrier at this size; x 0.75 for hydrodynamic retardation; MD (vacuum) shows sticking on every contact
J. N. Israelachvili, Intermolecular and Surface Forces, 3rd ed., Academic Press (2011), ch. 13
liquid-like below 1.18 nm at 348 K (Pawlow fit to EAM melting points, this work); 1.49 nm from Buffat & Borel 1976

necks form on every contact at all sizes 1.5-8 nm (irreversible, dPE < 0), but shape relaxation stalls more with size (Au residual xi after 2 ns ~0.3 at 1.5 nm, ~0.45 at 2-2.5 nm, ~0.6 at 3 nm, ~0.75 at 4-5 nm, ~0.85 at 6-8 nm; Ag higher at each size) and depends only weakly on T from 3 nm up: faceted, nucleation-limited regime
